source.text: Particle 1355 of the 2000 drawn with the seed 20261016 from the population of examples/synthetic-triso-population.json: the hottest kernel of the 2000 (kernel peak 978.387 K). Closed form of the layered sphere with constant conductivities: matrix 949.737 K, film 12.126 K, outer PyC 0.1997 K, SiC 0.0728 K, inner PyC 0.379 K, gap 0.2752 K, buffer 12.205 K, kernel parabola q R^2 / (6 k) = 3.391 K: the kernel centre is 978.3868 K, 16.523 K above the outer wall. The observed value is FEED's kernel centre, the first kernel cell plus the parabola's rise over the cell's radius. Tolerance 0.15 K = 0.5 % of the 16.523 K internal rise + the mesh bound 5 x 3.391 K / 48^2 = 0.0074 K + the wedge of the solver's mesh (the 2 degree wedge of the sphere with its radii times lambda = 0.999695, 48 cells in every region), which makes every drop lambda^2 = 0.999391 of the sphere's, rounded up to 0.05 K, fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own closed form (src/core/trisoSolve.ts, tests/seedOracleTriso.test.ts, to 1e-6 K) and FEED's finite-volume solution; the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1, tests/seedOracleTriso.test.ts) with every check of the run passing, and its saved output (tests/golden/seed-oracles-triso/) inside the tolerance.
